From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: MAP: Performance evaluation & HW sizing proposal (DataDock)

Hi Emma / team,

Thanks for the demo last week — great discussion. As promised, I put together a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the performance evaluation & hardware sizing you requested. Objective: validate production latency/throughput, TTFT (time-to-first-token), and concurrency profiles across candidate accelerators (A100, H100, L40S) and MIG vs full-GPU setups so you can finalize sizing for your Dedicated capacity commitment.

Summary (high level):
- Scope: sample workload (chat + completion) and embedding extraction for your catalog indexing pipeline.
- Models: open encoder-decoder family (we'll use a 13B-ish production-config: quantized + fp16 baseline).
- HW candidates: NVIDIA A100 (40GB/80GB variants), H100, L40S. Tests include full-GPU runs and common MIG slice sizes (1/2, 1/4 where supported).
- Metrics: median latency, p95/p99, throughput (tokens/sec), TTFT, concurrency (steady-state QPS and latency under load), GPU utilization, and cost-per-1M tokens estimate.
- Test matrix highlights: sequence lengths 512 / 2048 / 8192 tokens, batch sizes 1/4/8, concurrency ladder 1/4/8/16/32/64.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Baseline quick-run (3 business days): micro-benchmarks for each HW at your canonical prompts (we will run default fp16 and one quantized flavor).
- Full MAP (10 business days after baseline): exhaustive matrix + consolidated XLS/PDF with graphs and recommendations.
- Recommendation checkpoint & sizing proposal (1 business day after MAP): target to close by Jan 31 if the MAP aligns to your performance/cost targets.

What we need from you to start:
1) A sample of ~200 representative prompts (short/long) and an embedding sample (csv or newline JSON).
2) Preferred SLA/latency targets (e.g., p95 < 300ms for short-chat default).
3) Procurement window (dates) for any billing/PO steps.

Note on MIG vs full-GPU: we will include MIG runs to measure density/throughput tradeoffs and to produce a per-concurrency cost table. In our prior runs, MIG can increase density for many small concurrent sessions, but full GPUs typically win for heavy-context sequences or very low-latency single-session scenarios. The MAP will validate this for your exact workload.

Attached: RDW_MAP_template.xlsx (MAP checklist + runbook).

If you confirm sample data and procurement timing today, we can kick off the baseline run tomorrow.

Best,
Olga Petrov

Subject: Re: MAP: Performance evaluation & HW sizing proposal (DataDock)

Nice start. I've sketched a concrete runbook and test matrix for the baseline and the full MAP. Key notes for the runs: 

- Models/configs to test in this order: FP16 baseline, int8 quantized (q4_m), and a mixed-precision path (fp16 inference with int8 KV cache where available).
- Sequence lengths: 512, 2048, 8192; measure both generation-heavy prompts (avg 512 gen) and long-context retrieval cases (8k).
- Batch sizes per device: 1 / 4 / 8; concurrency ladder: 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64.
- TTFT: measure time from request receipt until first token on the wire (incl. prefix/kernel compile if cold). We'll capture cold vs warm-start TTFT.
- Throughput: tokens/sec over steady-state 60s windows after warm-up.
- Packing & KV caching: run with empty cache and with prefix-cached scenarios to model interactive sessions.
- MIG slices: for A100 & H100 we'll test 1/2 and 1/4 where vendor tooling permits. L40S usually used full; we'll evaluate smaller slices if available in our partner fleet.

Preliminary pass expectations (back-of-envelope):
- H100 ~ 1.3-1.6x throughput vs A100 in FP16 for heavy generation; L40S slightly lower latency for shorter contexts (good for low-latency single-session routing).
- MIG slices: per-slice throughput is ~30-60% of a full GPU divided by slice count, but density increases (useful for many small sessions).

I'll provision the benchmark harness and automation; Marissa can own data collection & plots. Olga, can you confirm we should include a cost-per-token calcs using Redwood-hosted pricing assumptions and an example Dedicated reserved tier?

-Karthik

Date: Tue, 18 Jan 2028 16:44:00 -0800
Subject: MAP results (baseline) & HW sizing recommendation — initial summary

Emma / team,

We completed the baseline runs and have an initial comparison summary attached (map-performance-results.xlsx and PDF summary). Below are the highlights and an actionable recommendation for sizing. Full MAP (full matrix + cost table) will be delivered end of week.

Executive highlights (baseline tests: short-chat prompts, 512-token context, avg generation 128 tokens):
- H100 (FP16, full GPU): median latency 120 ms, p95 240 ms, steady throughput ~150 tokens/sec per GPU at concurrency=8.
- A100 (FP16, full GPU): median latency 160 ms, p95 320 ms, steady throughput ~110 tokens/sec per GPU at concurrency=8.
- L40S (FP16, full GPU): median latency 100 ms, p95 260 ms, steady throughput ~140 tokens/sec per GPU at concurrency=8.
- MIG (1/4 slice on H100): per-slice throughput ~32 tokens/sec, density advantage: ~3.2x concurrent sessions per physical GPU vs full-GPU for light-weight chat. Cold TTFT impact: MIG slices show ~15-25% higher cold TTFT compared to full GPU on first request.

Notes & interpretation:
- L40S performed surprisingly well for short-context, low-latency workloads — good candidate for interactive routing when p95 constraints matter and your sessions are small.
- H100 leads on raw throughput for heavy generation and long-context workloads; it also scales better with larger batch sizes and longer sequences.
- A100 remains a cost-effective generalist but underperforms H100 on heavy generation.
- MIG is viable when you have many small concurrent sessions and want high density; not recommended as the primary option if you need consistent ultra-low cold TTFT for long-context generation.

Preliminary sizing recommendation (for target: 1k concurrent lightweight sessions with p95 < 300ms for short-chat):
- Option A (latency-first): 50 L40S nodes behind a routing policy that pins short-chat to L40S; keep H100s for heavy generation workloads (24 GPUs).
- Option B (throughput-first): H100 fleet (48 GPUs) with autoscaling and a small L40S pool for low-latency tail cases.

Next steps:
- We'll finish the full MAP (including 8k context & quantized runs) by Jan 21 and share the final XLS/PDF + cost-per-token estimates.
- Procurement: attached a one-page SOW template and DocuSign link (also uploaded to Drive). Please advise if you want edits to the SOW.

Attachments: map-performance-results.xlsx (detailed numbers), map-performance-results-summary.pdf, scheduler-diagram.png

If this aligns with your expectations, could we lock a trial Dedicated window Jan 22–26 to stress test a recommended candidate fleet? That will let you verify production routing behavior with your traffic.

Thanks — Olga
